feedback.details: SprintCriterion in shared/types.ts (line 55) has `type?: "behavioral" | "implementation"` — optional field with correct union type. SprintContract interface is unchanged. RegressionCriterion is a clean new interface. Backward compatible since type is optional.

CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_GENERATOR_PROMPT includes type field in JSON example and instructions to classify as 'behavioral' or 'implementation' (lines 386-412). CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_EVALUATOR_PROMPT validates type field presence (lines 414-425). Static prompts (PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT, GENERATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT, EVALUATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT) are unchanged.

In harness.ts line 662, after a sprint passes, `accumulateRegressionCriteria` is called. The function in regression.ts filters for `c.type === 'behavioral'` (line 37), excluding implementation and untyped criteria. Deduplication by name with Map (lines 43-56), newer replaces older.

regression.json is a JSON array of RegressionCriterion objects (name, description, threshold, sprintNumber). File created on first accumulation, appended on subsequent. cleanHarnessArtifacts (files.ts:68-76) only cleans contracts/, feedback/, spec.md, progress.json — regression.json is not touched.

In harness.ts lines 537-546, for sprint > 1 when noBdd is false, regression criteria are read and buildRegressionSection produces a '## Regression Criteria' header. This is appended to supplementaryContext which is injected into the evaluator prompt (evaluator.ts line 41). Empty criteria produce empty string (no section). Minor note: the condition `sprint > 1` means sprint 1 never gets regression injection, which is correct.

Both accumulation (harness.ts:662 `if (!config.noBdd)`) and injection (harness.ts:537 `if (!config.noBdd && sprint > 1)`) are guarded by noBdd flag. When noBdd is true, regression.json is not read, not written, and not deleted if it exists. Correct behavior.

static-analysis.ts detects 'lint', 'typecheck', 'type-check' keys from package.json scripts (line 4). Gracefully returns empty array on no package.json, no scripts field, or no matching keys (try/catch on line 28-31, scripts check on line 20). Reads from projectDir which is config.workDir or app/ for greenfield (harness.ts:868).

Commands are executed via Bun.spawnSync in harness.ts (line 885), between generator and evaluator. Output injected as '## Static Analysis Results' section (line 570). Non-zero exit codes don't prevent evaluator unless lintGate is set. Minor: uses Bun.spawnSync (sync) rather than async, but follows existing codebase patterns with execSync.

When no commands detected, runStaticAnalysis returns {output: '', failed: false} (harness.ts:877). The empty output check on line 551 means no '## Static Analysis Results' section is added. No error or warning is logged.

truncateStaticAnalysisOutput in static-analysis.ts (lines 38-42) truncates at 4000 chars with correct message format: '[output truncated — showing first 4000 chars of N total]'. Output at or below 4000 chars is returned unchanged. Applied in harness.ts line 908.

--lint-gate flag parsed in config.ts (line 95) as boolean, stored as `lintGate?: boolean` on HarnessConfig (line 42). When set and lint fails, evaluator is skipped (harness.ts:553-567), attempt counted as failed with `continue`, feedback includes lint output in overallSummary which is passed to Generator on next retry via lastEval.

regression.test.ts covers: (1) writing behavioral criteria, (2) excluding implementation criteria, (3) excluding no-type criteria, (4) deduplication by name, (5) reading/injecting via buildRegressionSection, (6) noBdd flag skipping (simulated conditional), (7) cleanHarnessArtifacts not deleting regression.json. All 6 describe blocks pass. The noBdd test is a simulation rather than integration but covers the pattern.

static-analysis.test.ts covers: (1) command detection for lint/typecheck/type-check keys, (2) empty array for no package.json, no scripts, no matching keys, (3) truncation at 4000 chars with correct message, (4) lint-gate logic tests (boolean pattern simulation). The lint-gate tests (lines 124-147) test only boolean logic patterns rather than actual harness integration, which is weak but covers the essential behavior contract.

All 311 tests pass across 16 files with 0 failures. All pre-existing test files (config, parse-eval-result, prompts, skills, logger, usage, extract-balanced-json, is-transient-error, parse-contract, documenter, harness-documenter, ensure-generator-commit, tracing, sprint3) continue to pass.

No 'any' type assertions in new code. Uses node:fs/promises (readFile, writeFile) in regression.ts. Static-analysis.ts uses readFile from node:fs/promises. Bun.spawnSync in harness is wrapped in try/catch (line 884-904). Named exports only, no default exports. Follows existing patterns consistently. The `as RegressionCriterion[]` cast on parsed JSON is reasonable and necessary.

evalResult.overallSummary: Sprint 1 is well-implemented. Both features (BDD Regression Accumulation and Static Analysis Soft Gate) are properly coded with correct integration in the harness loop. Types, prompts, config, regression logic, and static analysis detection/truncation are all solid. Tests are comprehensive (311 pass, 0 fail) with good coverage of the specified scenarios. The lint-gate tests are somewhat weak (testing boolean patterns rather than real integration) but cover the essential behavior. Code quality is clean with no 'any' assertions, proper error handling, and consistent style.

feedback.details: harness.ts lines 575-579 correctly compute diff on retry > 0, appending to supplementaryContext. computeDiffSection in shared/diff.ts properly generates the '## Changes Since Last Attempt' section. The diff is appended after regression and static analysis sections without overwriting them.
Double protection: harness.ts line 575 guards with `retry > 0`, and computeDiffSection itself returns undefined for attempt <= 0 (diff.ts line 17). No diff section appears on first attempt.

diff.ts lines 35-37 detect empty/whitespace-only diff output and return '[No changes detected]' within the section header. Test in diff.test.ts line 62-71 verifies this behavior explicitly, including checking it's not whitespace-only.

MAX_DIFF_CHARS = 8000 defined at line 3 of diff.ts. Lines 41-42 truncate and append '[diff truncated — showing first 8000 chars of N total]'. Test at line 73-85 creates a large file and verifies truncation behavior.

diff.ts catch block at line 29-32 returns undefined on any git failure. harness.ts lines 466-470 also catch git rev-parse failures gracefully. Tests cover no-git-repo (line 43-47) and invalid SHA (line 87-91) scenarios. Other supplementaryContext sections (regression, static analysis) are built independently before the diff section.

harness.ts lines 465-470 capture beforeSha via `git rev-parse HEAD` before the generator runs (the generator invocation starts at line 480). The diff is computed after generator completes (line 575-579) but before evaluator runs (line 582+).

Grep of generator.ts confirms no references to diffSection, computeDiffSection, or 'Changes Since Last Attempt'. supplementaryContext is only constructed and passed to runEvaluator (harness.ts line 599). The generator only receives lastEval feedback.

CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_GENERATOR_PROMPT (lines 394-421 of prompts.ts) explicitly mentions: 'naming conventions', 'code duplication', 'error handling patterns', 'maintainability', requires 'at least one criterion with type "implementation"', and specifies these as code quality criteria. Goes well beyond the generic 'code quality' that existed before.

CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_EVALUATOR_PROMPT (lines 423-436) explicitly states: 'If the contract contains ONLY behavioral/functional criteria and no quality criteria, you MUST reject it and add appropriate quality criteria.' Also specifies checking for at least one quality-focused implementation criterion.

Both prompts specify quality criteria should use type 'implementation'. The evaluator prompt at line 435 states: 'Quality criteria (naming, duplication, error handling, maintainability) should use type "implementation" so they do not accumulate in the regression set across sprints.' regression.ts line 37 confirms only behavioral criteria are carried forward.

buildEvaluatorPrompt includes a '## Quality Criteria' section (lines 198-204) stating quality criteria 'MUST be assessed with the same scoring rigor and threshold as behavioral/functional criteria. They are NOT optional or advisory.' Lists specific checks for naming, duplication, error handling, and maintainability.

tests/diff.test.ts covers all 5 required scenarios: (1) successful diff at line 49, (2) truncation at line 73, (3) graceful return undefined for no-git at line 43 and empty beforeSha at lines 33/38, (4) skipping on attempt 0 at line 28, (5) empty diff at line 62. Also includes invalid SHA test and attempt > 1 test. All 336 tests pass.

tests/quality-criteria.test.ts verifies generator prompt contains 'naming conventions', 'duplication', 'error handling patterns', 'maintainability', and type 'implementation'. Evaluator prompt tests verify 'reject', 'quality criteria', 'at least one'. buildEvaluatorPrompt tests verify 'same scoring rigor' and 'NOT optional'. All pass.
Running `bun test` produces 336 pass, 0 fail across 18 test files. No regressions detected.

Running `bunx tsc --noEmit` shows 11 errors, all in files not modified by this sprint (shared/artifact-digest.ts, tests/config.test.ts, tests/skills.test.ts — all pre-existing from prior sprints). No new TypeScript errors introduced. shared/diff.ts has proper type annotations (string | undefined return type, typed parameters).

evalResult.overallSummary: Sprint 2 is well-implemented. The diff-aware evaluation feature (Feature 1.3) is cleanly implemented in shared/diff.ts with proper integration in harness.ts. It handles all edge cases (first attempt, empty diff, truncation, git failures) gracefully. The quality criteria feature (Feature 1.4) properly updates both CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_GENERATOR_PROMPT and CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_EVALUATOR_PROMPT with specific quality criteria instructions and enforcement. The evaluator prompt includes a dedicated Quality Criteria section with rigorous scoring instructions. Tests are comprehensive and all pass. No new TypeScript errors or regressions were introduced.

feedback.details: --sprint is defined in parseCli() as type 'string' at line 99 of config.ts, parsed to number via parseInt at line 141, and exposed as 'sprint' on ParsedCli (line 58). Running with '--sprint 3' sets value to 3; omitting leaves undefined. Verified via runtime test.
HarnessConfig in shared/types.ts includes 'sprint?: number' at line 44. resolveConfig() maps cli.sprint to config.sprint at line 299. Both verified in source and via runtime test.

resolveConfig() at line 184 checks if both sprint and resume are set and throws 'Cannot use --sprint and --resume together.' This occurs before any workspace initialization or LLM calls. Verified via runtime test and unit tests.

sprintSelectionHarness at line 377 checks existsSync for spec.md and throws 'No spec found. Run the planner first or provide a spec.' when missing. This is before any planning/LLM invocation. Test coverage is via source-code string matching rather than behavioral test.

sprintSelectionHarness (lines 364-470) never calls runPlanner(). It loads spec via readSpec() at line 397 and proceeds directly to runSprintLoop(). Test at line 167-178 verifies the function body doesn't contain runPlanner() and does contain readSpec().

sprintSelectionHarness passes sprintN as both startSprint and endSprint (totalSprints param) to runSprintLoop at lines 460-461. The loop at line 521 runs 'for (sprint = startSprint; sprint <= totalSprints; sprint++)' so only sprint N executes. The log shows 'SPRINT N/N' (line 523). The denominator shows N/N rather than N/total which is slightly odd but functionally correct.

In the sprint loop at lines 536-542, when config.sprint is set, the code attempts readContract(config.workDir, sprint). If it exists, it's loaded with a log message 'Loaded existing contract for sprint'. Negotiation is skipped via the if(!contract) guard at line 545.

When readContract throws (no file exists), contract remains undefined. The if(!contract) block at line 545 triggers 'Negotiating sprint contract...' and runs negotiation. The logic is clear and correct.

At lines 410-421, when sprintN > 1, it reads progress and checks completedSprints >= sprintN - 1. If not (or if progress.json doesn't exist), it logs 'Warning: No checkpoint for sprint N-1. Ensure the codebase is in the expected state.' Execution continues without error.

resolveConfig at lines 189-193 rejects non-positive integers (0, NaN) with 'Invalid --sprint value'. For -1, Node's parseArgs itself rejects it as ambiguous, which is still a clear error but not the custom message. When sprint exceeds total sprints, line 406 logs a warning. Slightly imperfect for -1 case but functionally correct.

At line 203, the prompt-required check explicitly exempts sprint mode: 'if (!userPrompt && !cli.resume && cli.sprint === undefined)'. Verified via runtime test: --sprint 3 without a prompt produces config with empty userPrompt string.
sprintSelectionHarness at line 382 calls initWorkspace with { resume: true }, which preserves existing .adhd/ artifacts. This mirrors the resume path behavior.

The sprint loop at lines 666-676 loads regression criteria via readRegressionCriteria() and buildRegressionSection() for sprint > 1 when !config.noBdd. Since sprint mode uses the same runSprintLoop, this works for --sprint 3. However, there's no sprint-mode-specific test for this — it's verified by checking source strings.

sprint-selection.test.ts covers all required areas: CLI parsing, mutual exclusion, spec requirement, contract reuse, sprint range, checkpoint warning, validation, no-prompt, workspace preservation, regression, type safety, and sprint-exceeds-total. All 364 tests pass. However, many tests use source-code string matching (reading harness.ts and checking for substrings) rather than behavioral/unit testing with mocks. This is functional but fragile — renaming a log message would break tests without any real regression.

tsc --noEmit produces 11 errors, but NONE are in sprint-related files (types.ts, config.ts, harness.ts, sprint-selection.test.ts). The errors are in pre-existing files: artifact-digest.ts (3 errors), config.test.ts (1 error missing noDocs field from prior sprint), and skills.test.ts (7 errors missing documenter field from prior sprint). The sprint field is properly typed as optional throughout. All 364 tests pass with bun test. The pre-existing TS errors are a concern but don't affect this sprint's work.

evalResult.overallSummary: Sprint 3 (Sprint Selection) is well-implemented. The --sprint N flag is properly parsed, validated, and integrated into the harness flow. The sprintSelectionHarness function correctly skips planning, checks for existing spec, reuses contracts, warns about missing checkpoints, and runs only the targeted sprint. All 364 tests pass. The main weaknesses are: (1) many tests rely on source-code string matching rather than behavioral testing, making them fragile; (2) there are 11 pre-existing TypeScript errors from prior sprints that weren't cleaned up. Despite these issues, all criteria meet the threshold.
